judges.11.p1.b1.text: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor; he was the son of a prostitute

judges.11.p1.b2.text: You shall have no inheritance in our father’s house, because you are the son of another woman.

judges.11.p1.b3.text: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, …

judges.11.p1.b4.text: … where worthless men gathered around him and traveled with him.

judges.11.p2.b5.text: … the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob.

judges.11.p2.b6.text: Come … be our commander, so that we can fight against the Ammonites.

judges.11.p2.b7.text: Did you not hate me and expel me from my father’s house? Why then have you come to me now, when you are in distress?

judges.11.p2.b8.text: This is why we now turn to you, that you may go with us, fight the Ammonites, and become leader over all of us who live in Gilead.

judges.11.p3.b9.text: If you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them to me, will I really be your leader?

judges.11.p3.b10.text: The LORD is our witness if we do not do as you say.

judges.11.p3.b11.text: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their leader and commander.

judges.11.p3.b12.text: And Jephthah repeated all his terms in the presence of the LORD at Mizpah.

judges.11.p4.b13.text: What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?

judges.11.p4.b14.text: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, …

judges.11.p4.b15.text: When Israel came up out of Egypt, they seized my land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and all the way to the Jordan.

judges.11.p5.b17.text: This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or of the Ammonites.

judges.11.p5.b18.text: … and came to Kadesh. … Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let us pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom would not listen.

judges.11.p5.b19.text: … camped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the territory of Moab, since the Arnon was its border.

judges.11.p5.b20.text: But Sihon would not trust Israel to pass through his territory. So he gathered all his people, encamped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.

judges.11.p6.b21.text: Then the LORD, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, … seizing all the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

judges.11.p6.b22.text: Do you not possess whatever your god Chemosh grants you? So also, we possess whatever the LORD our God has granted us.

judges.11.p6.b23.text: I have not sinned against you, but you have done me wrong by waging war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites.

judges.11.p6.b24.text: But the king of the Ammonites paid no heed to the message Jephthah sent him.

judges.11.p7.b25.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah,

judges.11.p7.b26.text: and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, then through Mizpah of Gilead. And from there he advanced against the Ammonites.

judges.11.p7.b27.text: If indeed You will deliver the Ammonites into my hand,

judges.11.p7.b28.text: then whatever comes out the door of my house to greet me on my triumphant return from the Ammonites

judges.11.p7.b29.text: will belong to the LORD, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering.

judges.11.p8.b30.text: So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hand.

judges.11.p8.b31.text: With a great blow he devastated twenty cities from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith, as far as Abel-keramim.

judges.11.p8.b32.text: So the Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.

judges.11.p9.b33.text: And when Jephthah returned home to Mizpah, there was his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing! She was his only child; he had no son or daughter besides her.

judges.11.p9.b34.text: No! Not my daughter! You have brought me to my knees! You have brought great misery upon me,

judges.11.p9.b35.text: for I have given my word to the LORD and cannot take it back.

judges.11.p9.b36.text: My father … you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you have said, for the LORD has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites.

judges.11.p10.b37.text: Let me do this one thing: Let me wander for two months through the mountains with my friends and mourn my virginity.

judges.11.p10.b39.text: So she left with her friends and mourned her virginity upon the mountains.

judges.11.p10.b40.text: After two months, she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. And she had never had relations with a man.

judges.11.p10.b41.text: So it has become a custom in Israel that each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.
